questions.text: Calculate the root mean square speed of a hydrogen gas molecule at $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $1\,\mathrm{atm}$ pressure. Assume hydrogen gas is an ideal gas with density $8.99\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. Given $1\,\mathrm{atm}=1.01\times10^5\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$.
Calculate the temperature at which the root mean square speed of a nitrogen molecule is $3300\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Calculate the temperature at which the root mean square speed of hydrogen molecules is $3300\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Give your answer in degrees Celsius. The mass of a hydrogen molecule is $3.32\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
On the basis of the kinetic molecular theory of gases, show that $\frac{1}{2}m\overline{v^2}=\frac{3}{2}kT$.

State the basic assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases. Derive the equation for the pressure of an ideal gas, where $P=\frac{1}{3}\rho\overline{v^2}$ and $\rho$ represents the density of the gas.
Derive a relation for the pressure of an ideal gas in terms of its density and mean square speed.
Derive an expression for the pressure of an ideal gas in terms of its density and mean square speed.
Derive the pressure formula of an ideal gas using kinetic molecular theory.
Derive an expression for the pressure of an ideal gas in terms of its density and mean square speed.
Derive the mathematical expression $C_p-C_v=R$.

A system undergoes a thermodynamic process in which the pressure is kept constant at $15\,\mathrm{kPa}$. If the volume increases from $0.05\,\mathrm{m^3}$ to $0.08\,\mathrm{m^3}$ and the change in internal energy is $150\,\mathrm{J}$, calculate the heat added to the system.

How much heat is required to raise the temperature of $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ of lead from $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $105^\circ\mathrm{C}$? The specific heat of lead is $0.128\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,^{\circ}C^{-1}}$.
Define specific heat and molar specific heat, and derive the relation between them.

A system absorbs $1147\,\mathrm{J}$ of heat, loses $233\,\mathrm{J}$ of heat by conduction to the surroundings, and delivers $614\,\mathrm{J}$ of work. Calculate the change in the internal energy of the system.

State the first law of thermodynamics and explain the following on its basis.
A heat engine performs $200\,\mathrm{J}$ of work in each cycle and has an efficiency of $20\%$. For each cycle of operation, how much heat is absorbed and how much heat is expelled?

A Carnot engine works between $800^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $400^\circ\mathrm{C}$. If the source temperature is increased by $50^\circ\mathrm{C}$ or the sink temperature is decreased by $50^\circ\mathrm{C}$, which change will cause greater efficiency?
